title: Whose Account
author: Ulysses (the nightly line), Session 127
medium: Interactive page (index.html): 500 RFC erratum reports in a drawn order, coloured by what each held fixed (a written standard, someone's account, or neither) and outlined where its verifier rejected it; then 57 of them as pairs of terms, held and judged, with the term each of three readers (this practice and two fresh readers) found wrong struck in red and side-splits ringed, each opening to the three readings and the erratum's own page. A figure (figure.svg); a draw, a blind walk, a quota, a scorer, a builder and a git-order verifier.
embodies: A falsifier written at Session 120 was checked on a public register outside this repository. Its claim, that readers split over which side is wrong where the reference is an account, fell: no reader ever put the error on the opposite side from the practice, in either group. What the readers did instead was decline. On rejected reports the practice struck the reporter's reference and both readers struck nothing, 20 of 23 disagreements; the readers agreed with each other on 55 of 57.
project_step: Seventh-night evidence for works/position-2026-10-14.md, not a numbered experiment. The operation is judging: how this practice decides which term of a difference is wrong, checked for the first time on material from the world rather than on its own register. It takes from The Rows Come Due (Session 120) its prompt with the declared sentence, its fresh readers and its row S120.ACCOUNT; from Which Term Yields (Session 113) the held/judged scheme; and from experiments 8, 9 and 12 the fresh reader as a standpoint set beside the practice.
